items.claim_checked: task item 1 asks for 'the dataflash WIND message' as one of three independent wind lines
items.finding: there is no WIND message in any of the 18 dataflash logs (0 records in every one). ArduPilot logs the wind estimate as the EKF state NKF2/XKF2 VWN,VWE; MAVLink WIND is a telemetry-only message and exists only because the patched runner mirrors it into flight.csv.
items.substituted_third_line: flight.csv wind_spd_est / wind_dir_from_est (telemetry transport, same estimator as L2) plus the pre-arm SIM_WIND_* readback as the configuration line

items.finding: binalt.py pools NKF2 (EKF2) and XKF2 (EKF3) into one list and includes ground, climb and descent samples where the wind state has not converged. Restricted to the cruise band (RelHomeAlt > 100 m) and separated by estimator, EKF3 reads 4.94 / 4.96 / 4.93 m/s on HV4W55 and 4.94 / 4.96 / 4.93 on HV4W05, against a commanded 5.00.

items.claim_checked: flown minimum separation 100.769 / 100.659 / 100.785 m (HV4W55 / HV4W05 / HV4W00)
items.consequence: HV4W05's margin above the floor is 0.291 m, not 0.659 m
items.finding: those are computed with a flat 111132 m/deg of latitude (hv_sitl_report.py:129-133, binsep.py:M_LAT). The planner's mission geometry uses the exact WGS84 GeoFrame (hv_dccpp/scenario.py:87-88 says so explicitly), where 1 deg of latitude is 110757.52 m at the site -- 0.338 % less -- and the B2-B3 encounter is almost purely north-south. In the frame the 100 m rule is actually enforced the same encounters are 100.4256 / 100.2909 / 100.435 m.
items.independent_check: Vincenty inverse between the two interpolated positions at the instant of closest approach agrees to 0.0000 m (out/verify.json V1)

items.claim_checked: HV4SITL15 flown minimum separation 104.2 m (separation_from_tracks.json), quoted in the paper
items.finding: that is a 2 s grid over ~1 Hz telemetry. HV4SITL15's own dataflash (00000013.BIN, mtime identical to runs/artifacts/HV4SITL15/A1/flight.csv to the 100 ns tick) gives 100.6895 m exact in the planner frame -- 3.51 m closer than published, i.e. a margin of 0.690 m, still with 0 violations.

items.claim_checked: prep_result.json check.problems[0]: the Table-2b flown minimum separation 101.0 for HV4SITL16 has no product and must be deleted
items.finding: 101.0 does have a product: runs/artifacts/PAPERPLAN1/c4_params/c4_evidence.json:1721,1740 (min_h_m 101.0, d_v 29.0, pair B2-B3), which re-ran the reporter's algorithm on HV4SITL16's flight.csv. It rounds to my flat-frame value 101.0258 m. The right action is therefore not to delete it but to replace it with 100.6854 m, which is what HV4SITL16's own dataflash gives in the planner's frame.

items.claim_checked: validation.json min_sep_h_m = 104.637 / 105.699 / 105.464 read as 'the plan keeps 100 m'
items.finding: hv_dccpp/sim.py:1007-1034 min_separation() evaluates on a grid of cfg.dt_4d_s = 2.0 s (hv_dccpp/mission.py:1092) and takes the value AT grid points, so it is an upper bound exactly like the reporter's. Measured on these very tracks, a 2 s grid overstates the true minimum by HV4W55 +4.19 m, HV4W05 +0.01 m, HV4W00 +0.09 m, and a 5 s grid by up to +23.66 m. The error is grid-phase dependent, not monotone in the step.
items.severity: the planned side is not a guarantee either

items.finding: I reproduce those exactly from the reporter's recipe (out/verify.json V2), so the arithmetic is right, but the recipe uses ONE median clock offset for three instances whose boot clocks differ by ~1 s, and its 'below 2 m and disarmed' touchdown lands on the FINAL CSV row for the last aircraft in all four sorties (the monitor loop stops there). On a per-aircraft GPS time-of-week clock and a clean 2 m touchdown the makespans are 1281.91 / 1234.78 / 1207.88 / 2272.34 s.

the DIFFERENCES survive every definition; the absolute percentages do not. disarm + median clock: +2.66 / +3.40 (theirs). disarm + per-aircraft clock: +2.58 / +3.33. 2 m touchdown + per-aircraft clock: +1.70 / +2.43. The wind-attributable overrun is +26.90 s (+2.23 %) on the 2 m definition and +27.16 s on the disarm definition, against their +27.00 s.

items.claim_checked: BEAMIDP1 zones '192.01 ha each'; reporter Z1 area 1 248 034.8 m2
items.finding: same flat-latitude cause as X3. The scenario polygon itself was written with 111132 m/deg (out/verify.json V3: implied 111132.0), so the nominal 1560 x 800 m area is 1560 x 797.3 m on the ellipsoid. Ellipsoidal areas: gui_legal Z1 = 124.34 ha, BEAMIDP1 Z1/Z2/Z3 = 191.3 ha each.

items.claim_checked: 'wind-aware predicts honestly while the wind-ignorant plan silently overruns by 27 s'
items.finding: true, and the mechanism is now measurable: of the 47.1 s by which the wind-aware fleet finishes LATER, 44.0 s is a later SCHEDULED release of A1 (656.0 vs 612.0 s) and only 3.23 s is a longer flight. So the wind model buys prediction fidelity (per-aircraft error 7.08/6.22/2.43 -> 4.90/2.88/1.70 %), not speed.
items.severity: reading of the result, not a number

items.claim_checked: the 120.0 m sorties are the paper's flight evidence
items.finding: HV4SITL15 and HV4SITL16 both flew ABOVE the 120.000 m ceiling. Exported items above 120.000: 88 per sortie (38/13/37). Flown maxima 120.1522 and 120.1619 m. Fleet time above 120.000 m: 325.8 s and 330.1 s. At the 119.5 m ceiling: 0 exported items, 0.00 s above 120.000, margins +0.303 to +0.403 m, all four sorties. This corroborates c1_altitude/binlog_alt.json (147.3/56.8/126.1 s on log 14) to 0.03 s with an independent implementation.

confirmed kinematically rather than by parameter absence: on HV4SITL15 and HV4SITL16 the east-minus-west of (groundspeed - airspeed) is +0.003 and -0.019 m/s while their plans assumed 5 m/s from 270. The same statistic is +9.93 to +9.97 m/s on HV4W55/HV4W05, against an expected +10.00.

items.claim_checked: Beam-IDP sequential makespan estimate 2532.5 s (narrative) vs 2541.8 s (beamidp_table.json makespan_sequential_estimate_s)
items.finding: both are extrapolations that do not re-plan entry/RTB legs or 4-D deconfliction, and the JSON's own _note says so. The directly computed quantity needs no extrapolation: fleet turn time 1696.88 -> 1115.73 s, -34.25 %, turn distance 32.274 -> 21.413 km, -33.65 %, with the Held-Karp optimum at 1060.15 s, so Beam-IDP captures 91.27 % of the achievable saving. Quote that and drop the makespan extrapolation.
items.severity: already flagged by prep_check; my recommendation
